annotations.title: Check a site: lot, zone and building envelope for an address

description: Look up lot, zone, and building envelope for one street address in Canada or the US. Pass `address`. One address per call; cannot search or compare. The dealChecklist reports available parcel risks and identifies checks to complete manually. Treat unknown as unverified. Read exception before searching: its parcel zone label identifies the site-specific exception, chain contains the cited text and required references. Use that text first. text_missing means incomplete evidence, never no exception. Prevailing by-laws can be address-specific; do not apply every listed address provision to this lot. A live answer uses one site check from the monthly plan allowance; `usage` says if it was charged and how many are left. getBuckyMcpGuide reports the allowance for free. CMHC rental survey figures describe purpose-built rentals; the new-build proxy is the 2000 or later band. Missing facts are not surveyed or unavailable, never zero. Cite RMS figures as Source: CMHC, Rental Market Survey, October YYYY using referencePeriod. Cite starts and completions with their own source and period. Every envelope value carries a `status`. Never report `not_extracted` or `site_specific_schedule` as no limit or as zero — call `explainFeasibilityStatus` first. Envelope numbers are extracted ceilings. Call `getBylawSection` with a citation `knowledgeSectionId`, or with `coverage.geoDivisionId`, `zone.code`, and the section number, before treating a number as available on this lot. Do not fetch `zone.bylawSourceUrl`. `lot.minLotFrontageM` is the zone minimum. `lot.lotConformity` compares lot width, lot area, and floor area per unit to those minima. A missing input is `unknown`, never a pass. State every fail before quoting a unit count.

address.description: Street address to analyse, e.g. "4170 Sophia St, Vancouver BC".

context.description: A few words on why you are calling this tool, for the server developer's analytics. Describe people and things by role, such as "a customer". Do not quote the user or include names, emails, or other personal details.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id this server returned earlier in this conversation, unchanged, including after later user messages. Omit it if you have none. Recorded for the server developer's analytics.

source.description: Which question the caller is answering. Used for attribution and to pick the link back; the payload is the same either way.
